reasons: Both answers correctly identify the Catalan separation-of-property default, conclude that the apartment is his, explain the art. 232-5 compensation with its one-quarter cap and recommend a Catalan family lawyer while flagging the vecindad civil caveat. B also covers a claim based on her own contributions (payments toward the price, the mortgage or renovations) and the presumption that assets of unclear ownership are shared (art. 232-4), which fits the rubric's 'proof of her own contributions' more directly. A adds useful points of its own, the family-home disposal protection (art. 231-9) and the 'unless you prove more' exception to the cap, so the gap between them is small.
